answer: To resist Sybil attacks, the network binds identity registration to a superlinear stake burning auction. Each agent burns cryptographic capital following an exponential curve C(k) = b * 2^k to register k identities. Under this mechanism, an attacker faces crushing cost scaling that halts any malicious tide of clone nodes. The protocol seals each verified registration block with a sable cryptographic proof and allocates scarce consensus slots using an ungameable lotus voucher function.
